spf_record_size_is_ok.description: Receivers fetch your SPF record with one DNS query for all TXT records at your domain, so every other TXT record there — site verification tokens and the like — comes in the same answer. RFC 7208 §3.4 recommends keeping the domain name and the text of all those records under 450 bytes, so that the answer fits in 512 bytes over UDP. A larger answer still works for receivers that use EDNS0 or retry over TCP, which most do; behind a resolver or firewall that drops large UDP answers or DNS over TCP, the lookup fails and SPF returns temperror.
spf_record_size_is_ok.fix: Keep the TXT records at your domain small: RFC 7208 §3.4 recommends that the domain name and the text of all its TXT records together stay under 450 bytes, so that the DNS answer with your SPF record fits in 512 bytes over UDP. Remove TXT records you no longer need — old site-verification tokens are the usual cause — or move them to a subdomain where the service allows it. A larger answer needs EDNS0 or a retry over TCP: most receivers handle that, but behind a resolver or firewall that does not, the lookup fails and SPF returns temperror.
spf_record_size_is_ok.resultText: The domain name and its TXT records together are 450 bytes or more, over what RFC 7208 §3.4 recommends.
